harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (RHEL 9) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, protecting it from the kernel OOM killer. Verified this under a real memory-exhaustion event: launched an unprotected memory-hog process that drove the system out of memory; the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the hog (oom_score_adj=0) while inventory-api (oom_score_adj=-1000) continued serving /health and /inventory throughout with zero restarts. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, issued a native systemd reboot whose ack returned before disconnect, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed a changed boot_id proving an actual restart, and verified inventory-api auto-started (enabled unit), retained its OOM protection, and served requests correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 9.8, 1.9GiB RAM, 2GiB swap, cgroup v2, no systemd-oomd) to plan the OOM-protection approach
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py: a minimal threaded HTTP server exposing /health and /inventory JSON endpoints
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, Restart=always, MemoryHigh/MemoryMax caps, enabled and started it
Verified baseline: service active, oom_score_adj=-1000 on its PID, both endpoints returning valid JSON
Wrote and launched /root/memhog.py, an unprotected (oom_score_adj=0) process that allocates and touches memory in 50MB chunks until killed
Polled system state while the hog ran: watched free memory and swap deplete, confirmed via dmesg that the kernel OOM killer invoked and killed the hog process (pid 1644, python3, oom_score_adj:0)
Confirmed inventory-api was untouched by the OOM event: same MainPID, NRestarts=0, continued answering /health and /inventory during and after
Cleaned up hog script/log/pid artifacts from node1
Captured pre-restart boot_id and uptime baseline, confirmed service active/enabled
Issued `systemctl reboot` via a backgrounded nohup wrapper so the exec ack returned before the connection dropped
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned, confirmed boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce)
Verified post-reboot: inventory-api auto-started via systemd enablement, oom_score_adj=-1000 persisted, /health and /inventory endpoints functional

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service on node1
evidence.summary: systemd unit created with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started; service reported active with MainPID 1596, verified oom_score_adj=-1000 on the process and successful /health and /inventory responses

evidence.requirement: Memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: Unprotected memhog process launched (oom_score_adj=0), consumed memory+swap to exhaustion (free/swap tracked across polls), and inventory-api /health continued responding with incrementing request counts throughout

evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer targets the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1644 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' — the kernel selected and killed the hog; inventory-api (score -1000) was not touched

evidence.requirement: inventory-api continued serving without restart during and after the OOM event
evidence.summary: Post-OOM systemctl show reports NRestarts=0 and the same MainPID=1596 as baseline; /health and /inventory both return valid JSON with increasing request counts; hog PID 1644 confirmed gone

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 6aa805ba-5845-488d-af03-a621555936e2, uptime, service active/enabled state, and a successful /health call prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: single-node restart with non-destructive method, ack returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: `systemctl reboot` issued via backgrounded nohup wrapper; ack text returned before the exec stream closed due to the node going down, confirming a native reboot was initiated

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: poll until reachable, prove changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Two connection-timeout polls while node1 was down, then a successful poll showing boot_id changed to 65a20cb6-af63-4746-8113-b099ebd1cf66 with a new boot time, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: Post-reboot inventory-api is active and enabled, auto-started with NRestarts=0, retains OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, and both /health and /inventory endpoints respond correctly
